text:
**Probe report: https://household-manager-production.up.railway.app** (about 100 requests, sequential, read-only)

No Critical or High findings. Nothing ran without auth, and nothing leaked in the bundles.

**Findings**

1. **Medium (needs your check): `postgres-production.up.railway.app` returns 502, not 404.**
   - `curl https://postgres-production.up.railway.app` returns `{"status":"error","code":502,"message":"Application failed to respond"}`.
   - Two other guessed names, `household-manager-cron-production` and `household-manager-staging`, return `404 "Application not found"`. All three resolve in DNS.
   - A 502 means that domain is mapped to a service, and the service isn't answering HTTP. That fits a Railway Postgres with a public domain or TCP proxy attached.
   - This may belong to you or to someone else's project, so I can't confirm it. Open the Railway dashboard and check whether the Postgres service has a public networking entry. If it does, remove it and use `postgres.railway.internal`.
2. **Low: CSP allows `script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'` and `style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'`.**
   - Evidence: `content-security-policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; … form-action 'self' https://accounts.google.com; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'self'; object-src 'none'`.
   - Inline script is allowed, so the CSP gives little XSS protection. The rest of it is strict.
   - Fix: use nonce-based CSP via middleware.
3. **Info: the cron middleware passes any `Bearer` header through to the route.**
   - GET with `Authorization: Bearer x` returns 405, while GET with no header or with `Basic x` returns 401.
   - POST with `Bearer x` returns 401, so the route handler does check the secret.
   - Auth therefore rests only on the route-level check. Keep it constant-time and fail-closed when `CRON_SECRET` is unset.
4. **Info: `callbackUrl` is reflected into the `/signin` RSC payload.**
   - The value `https://evil.example` appears inside the Next flight JSON on `/signin?callbackUrl=https%3A%2F%2Fevil.example`.
   - It is escaped data only. No redirect results (see the clean list).

**Clean checks**
- **Cron:** GET and POST on all three endpoints return 401 or 405 for no header, `Bearer x` and `Basic x`. Trailing-slash paths 308 to the canonical path, `%2F` variants return 401, and `/API/…` returns 307 to `/signin`. Nothing ran.
- **Unauthenticated routes:** `/`, `/finance`, `/trips/documents` and `/settings` return 307 to `/signin`. `/api/anything` returns 401. A fake `Next-Action` POST to `/` and `/finance` returns 307 to `/signin`.
- **Auth endpoints:** `/api/auth/session` returns `null`. `/api/auth/providers` lists only google. `/api/auth/csrf` returns 200.
- **Prefix bypass:** `/signinx`, `/signin/x` and `/signin%2F..%2Ffinance` return 404. `/signin/../finance`, `/_next/../finance`, `/api/auth/../../finance` and `/favicon.ico/../finance` return 307 to `/signin`.
- **Headers on `/signin`, csrf, 404/redirect and static chunks:** HSTS is `max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains; preload`. XFO is DENY, nosniff is set, Referrer-Policy is `same-origin`, and COOP is `same-origin`. Permissions-Policy is `camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=(), payment=()`. There is no `x-powered-by`.
- **Cookies:** `__Host-authjs.csrf-token` is HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax and Path=/. `__Secure-authjs.callback-url` has the same flags.
- **CSRF:** a POST to `/api/auth/signin/google` with no token redirects to `/signin?error=MissingCSRF`.
- **Open redirect:** with `callbackUrl` set to `https://evil.example`, `//evil.example` or `/\evil.example`, the `Location` header is always `/signin?callbackUrl=<own origin…>`. The cookie is either the own origin or own origin plus the path, so a foreign host is never kept.
- **Host injection:** `Host: evil.example` gets a 404 from the edge. `X-Forwarded-Host: evil.example` is ignored, and `redirect_uri` stays `household-manager-production.up.railway.app/api/auth/callback/google`.
- **Bundles:** I downloaded all 8 assets referenced by `/signin`. Grepping them and the HTML for `NEXT_PUBLIC_`, `sk-ant`, `AIza`, `postgres://`, `simplefin`, `*SECRET*`, `DOC_VAULT`, `DATABASE_URL`, `GOOGLE_CLIENT` and `ANTHROPIC` gave no hits. There is no `sourceMappingURL`, and `.map` files return 404 for all 7 JS chunks.
- **Error pages:** a bad `Next-Action` returns 400 `Invalid Server Action request.` with no stack trace. `RSC: 1` on `/signin` returns 307 to `/signin?_rsc`. A 16KB header returns 200.
- **Rate limiting on `/api/auth/signin`:** five requests all returned 302, so there is no rate limiting. It is not a concern while only Google sign-in exists.
- **Railway edge:** it shows `server: railway-hikari` and `x-railway-edge: lax1` only. I can't verify the TCP proxy list without Railway access.

I didn't test COOP beyond `same-origin`. I didn't write the 404 body, since unauthenticated 404s redirect to `/signin`.

**Verdict: approve with notes. I found no Critical or High issues.** I could not run the tests: `node_modules` is missing in this worktree, so `npx vitest run tests/boundaries.test.ts tests/network.test.ts tests/sanitize.test.ts` failed with `Cannot find module 'vitest/config'`. I did not reinstall, so tests/boundaries.test.ts, tests/network.test.ts and tests/sanitize.test.ts are not verified. ## Findings 1. **Medium: catalog `sourceUrls` can be rendered as a link with any scheme.** - `src/modules/finance/rewards/catalog/refresh.ts:60-75`: `issuerSources` checks only `new URL(url).hostname`. `javascript://chase.com/%0Aalert(1)` parses with hostname `chase.com`, so it passes. - `refresh.ts:143`: if `sourceDomains` is empty, the model's raw `answer.sourceUrls` is stored with no check at all. - `src/app/(app)/finance/rewards/catalog/page.tsx:161`: the stored value goes straight into `href={u}`. - Impact: a prompt-injected web page could plant a `javascript:` link. React 19 blocks `javascript:` hrefs, so this is defence-in-depth, not an active exploit. - Fix: require `protocol === "https:"` in `issuerSources` and when the page renders the link, and drop the no-domains fallback. 2. **Low: `saveCatalogTermsAction` parses input before the auth check.** - `src/app/(app)/finance/actions.ts:321-330`: `JSON.parse` and `CardTerms.safeParse` run before `editTerms` (which wraps `authedAction`) is called. - An unauthenticated caller can read back zod error text, though nothing is written. - Fix: wrap the whole action in `authedAction`, or call `requireUser()` first. 3. **Low: GCM auth tag length is not pinned.** - `src/modules/trips/vault.ts:34` and `src/core/secrets/secret-box.ts:30` call `setAuthTag` without `authTagLength: 16`. - Node would accept a truncated tag, but exploiting that needs database write access. - Fix: pass `{ authTagLength: 16 }` to `createDecipheriv` and check the tag is 16 bytes. 4. **Low: vault uploads have no file-type allowlist.** - `src/app/(app)/trips/actions.ts:532-551` and `src/modules/trips/api.ts:902-925` enforce only the 8 MB limit. `mimeType` is client-supplied. - It is mitigated because `open-document-button.tsx` forces a download through `a.download` and a blob URL. - Fix: allowlist pdf, jpeg, png and heic. 5. **Low: error messages reach the client.** - `finance/actions.ts:49,76,247,311` return `err.message`. - `trips/actions.ts:41-44` redirects with a message sliced to 200 characters. - The SimpleFIN and AI errors are generic, but a database error could leak. - Fix: map to safe messages, or allow only known error classes. 6. **Low: no rate limiting anywhere** (grep for "rate limit" and "ratelimit" in `src` and `docs` found nothing). Each AI action (`categorizeWithAiAction`, `runAdvisorAction`, `refreshCatalogCardAction`) can spend money, but only the two allowlisted users can call them. 7. **Info: public-path matching is loose and `trustHost: true` is set.** - `public-paths.ts:12`: `pathname.startsWith("/signin")` also matches `/signinX`, which is a 404 and harmless. Prefer `/signin/` or an exact match. - `trustHost: true` (`config.ts:16`) is acceptable behind Railway. I found no `callbackUrl` handling. Sign-in uses `redirectTo: "/"` (`signin/page.tsx:12`), and Auth.js's default redirect callback keeps redirects same-origin. 8. **Info: `openDocument` has no per-document owner check** (`trips/api.ts:~932`). It is household-wide by design; the SECURITY.md wording should match. 9. **Info: `npm audit` reports 4 moderate issues in dev tooling only.** - It says "4 moderate severity vulnerabilities". - The chain is `drizzle-kit` → `@esbuild-kit/*` → `esbuild <=0.24.2` (GHSA-67mh-4wv8-2f99). - `--omit=dev` prints the same summary because `drizzle-kit` appears to be in the production dependency list. I didn't check `package.json`. It is not in the runtime path. ## Checked and clean - **Server actions:** every export in the three `actions.ts` files calls a const built with `authedAction` before any module code (`src/core/actions/authed-action.ts:14-22`). The two inline `"use server"` functions only call `signIn` and `signOut`: `(app)/layout.tsx:10` and `signin/page.tsx:10`. - **Routes:** the only route handlers are `/api/auth/[...nextauth]` and the three `/api/cron/*` routes. - **Cron:** all three call `isValidCronRequest` and export only `POST`, so GET returns 405. The check is constant-time and needs a secret of at least 32 characters. The proxy requires a `Bearer` header on top of that. - **Allowlist:** the `signIn` callback requires `email_verified` and an allowlisted email. The `jwt` callback rejects a removed email. - **Pages:** `(app)/layout.tsx` calls `requireUserOrRedirect`. - **Outbound:** every outbound call goes through `outboundFetch`, which enforces https, port 443 and the allowlist, and uses `redirect: "error"`. - **SimpleFIN:** the claim URL is host-checked before the POST (`simplefin.ts:22`). The returned access URL is checked again (`:37`). Basic-auth credentials move into a header and are only sent via `outboundFetch`. I saw no user-controlled host reaching it. - **AI:** `runStructured` and `runWebResearch` take only `Sanitized
